Definition: from G303 and G3973; (reflexively) to repose (literally or figuratively (be exempt), remain); by implication, to refresh:--take ease, refresh, (give, take) rest.
BiblicalUsage: Jesus says, 'Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest' — and He tells His disciples to come apart into a desert place and rest a while, for there were many coming and going. Paul tells Philemon the bowels of the saints are refreshed by his love, and the voice from heaven says blessed are the dead which die in the Lord, that they may rest from their labours. The word is rest, refreshment, and the laying down of a burden — given by Christ, shared among the saints, and finished in death.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe rest is a gift before it is a duty: Jesus gives it to the heavy laden, the disciples take it apart from the crowds, the saints refresh one another with love, and the dead rest from their labours. I hold that the rest He gives now is the same rest the voice promises at the end — not an escape from work, but the end of labouring without Him.
